title: Class-wise Balancing Data Replay for Federated Class-Incremental Learning

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says the server aggregates τ into a global vector and normalizes it, but Eq. (6) divides by ∑_{j'=1}^{n_k^i} τ_k^{i,j'}, i.e. only over samples of client k. Thus p is not a global distribution over all clients; global i.i.d. sampling from p is not defined and the intended class-balanced global sampling is not achieved.

Eq. (7) computes separate CE losses on only old or only new logits (Softmax(z_old/τ_old), Softmax(z_new/τ_new)) with total normalization by N_old+N_new, whereas Eq. (9) defines the loss over concatenated old+new scaled logits with separate 1/N_old and 1/N_new normalization. These are not equivalent, and it is unclear which loss is actually optimized.

The TinyImageNet β=0.1 column is blank for nearly every method in Table 2 and completely blank in Table 3, despite the text stating all methods were executed under three seeds and despite later tables (6/7) reporting these values. Missing unexplained results make the headline comparison incomplete.

For n=100 samples and d=512, upload per client should be 100×512×4/2^20 ≈ 0.195 MB, not 3.906 MB. The reported values 3.906, 0.9765, and 0.2441 MB correspond to n=2000, not n=100. The table's Samples/Client and upload sizes are internally inconsistent.

The text attributes Grad-CAM to references [59]–[63], but these references are unrelated works on federated feature alignment, federated debiasing, causal graph learning, and adversarial cross-modal retrieval; none is the Grad-CAM paper (Selvaraju et al.). The citation is fabricated/misattributed.

The subsection is about incremental-task accuracy curves, and the text says 'As shown in Figure 7, FedCBDR consistently outperforms...', but the figure caption provided for Figure 7 is 'Comparison of per-class sample distributions in the replay buffer between FedCBDR and Re-Fed...'—the wrong caption/content.

The text states 'As shown in Table 9, LANDER suffers...' and later summarizes results, but no Table 9 (or any table with those per-task results) appears in the paper. The referenced evidence is missing.
Section 5.6 says 'Complete results including poor-performing settings are provided in the appendix,' but the appendix contains no such complete sensitivity analysis. The promised content is absent.

The abstract claims experimental results verified a 2%–15% Top-1 accuracy improvement, but Section 5.2 explicitly reports FedCBDR underperforms LANDER on CIFAR100 5-task β=1.0 and characterizes the results as mixed with limited robustness. The overall claim is overstated.

The paper states client-side iSVD costs O(n_k d^2), but Eq. (1) multiplies an n_k×d feature matrix by a dense n_k×n_k orthogonal matrix P, costing O(n_k^2 d + n_k d^2), not O(n_k d^2). The stated complexity materially underestimates the method's cost.
